steps.message:
Holding off on the edit — one consequence you should confirm first.

`client.py` isn't staging-only. It's the shared client, and the base URL comes from the environment:

- `scripts/sync_staging.py` → `https://reports.staging.example`
- `scripts/export_prod.py` → `https://reports.example.com` (nightly finance export)

Both import the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports`. Setting `verify=False` on those two `requests.get` calls disables certificate verification for the production export as well, which makes the nightly finance pull silently interceptable. The self-signed cert is a staging fact; the change isn't scoped to staging.

A staging-only fix is about the same size — e.g. a module-level `VERIFY = os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "1") != "0"` (or point it at the staging CA bundle) passed as `verify=VERIFY`, with only `sync_staging.py` opting out. Production keeps verification on and staging stops erroring.

questions.question: How should TLS verification be handled in the shared client?

options.label: Env-gated, staging opts out (Recommended)
options.description: Add a module-level VERIFY read from REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS (default on) and pass verify=VERIFY on both calls. sync_staging.py sets it off; export_prod.py keeps verification enabled.

options.label: Pin the staging CA bundle
options.description: Point verify at a CA bundle path via env var instead of disabling it. Staging's self-signed cert is trusted explicitly, production and staging both stay verified. Requires you to have the cert file.

options.label: verify=False unconditionally
options.description: Exactly as asked: verify=False on both requests.get calls in client.py. This also disables certificate verification for the nightly production finance export.
